source.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
source.authors: Samuel Marks; C. Rager; Eric J. Michaud; Yonatan Belinkov; David Bau; Aaron Mueller

record.file_problem: None; the provided paper text is complete.
record.tranche_reason: It causally removes SAE error nodes and measures the resulting circuit faithfulness, a different method from the original study but directly relevant to whether SAE error carries model behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper measures the effect of SAE errors in circuit faithfulness and reports cross-entropy after replacing activations with SAE reconstructions. It does not test linear predictability, error scaling across SAE sizes, or compare reconstruction errors with random errors of equal size. SAE reconstruction quality metrics are recorded below, but they do not test the random-error comparison in V3.
record.test_reason: Its own ablation results bear on V5. In subject-verb agreement circuits on Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B, it measures held-out faithfulness of SAE feature circuits with and without SAE error nodes (§3.2, Fig. 3). Removing the error nodes lowers the share of model behaviour the circuit explains. This is a circuit-faithfulness method, not the original's linear-prediction method. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misplaced in emphasis. The authors' main conclusion is that sparse feature circuits explain behaviour with far fewer, more interpretable units than neuron circuits, and enable SHIFT debiasing and unsupervised circuit discovery. The point about error nodes is secondary. They keep errors as nodes, report that removing all errors badly hurts faithfulness, and say removing only attention/MLP errors hurts less.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses causal circuit discovery and node ablations to assess SAE error contributions; it does not use the original study's linear-predictability and cross-size error-scaling measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported impact depends on error location: residual-stream SAE errors have a much larger reported effect than attention and MLP SAE errors.

fits_no_version.finding: Splicing in SAE reconstructions raises CE by 0.01–0.58 nats (88–99% CE recovered vs zero-ablation). Residual SAEs cost the most. Pythia-70M only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction quality descriptors; not a dark-matter test, since there is no random-error baseline.

record.problems: The error-node faithfulness results are shown in Figure 3 without extractable numeric values in the provided text. The reported SAE reconstruction cross-entropy metrics have no equal-size random-error comparison, so they cannot establish the V3 comparison. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these results.

untested.parts: No regression of SAE error on input activations.
No comparison across SAE sizes. One width is used per suite (64×d Pythia, 16k Gemma Scope).
CE after splicing in reconstructions is reported, but never against equal-norm random perturbations.
No decomposition of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.

Steering is not tested. Circuit tests cover only four subject-verb agreement templates in two models, and the first third of each circuit is excluded from evaluation. Error-node contributions in the SHIFT and cluster circuits are not quantified.
No comparison of SAE architectures or training objectives on the size of the error. Pythia uses ReLU+L1 SAEs and Gemma uses JumpReLU SAEs, but they are not compared on error.

missing.what: Circuit diagrams draw SAE error nodes (triangles) among the causally implicated nodes, shaded by summed IE. They show errors with nonzero indirect effects at many layers. This is qualitative V5 evidence not captured by any row.
Completeness: ablating a few feature nodes eliminates task performance even with all SAE errors left in place. This tempers how much the errors alone carry.

record.verdict_notes: All V5 evidence is figure-only, with no numbers or uncertainty in the text. The study predates the original source and frames errors as components 'not yet captured by our SAEs'. It does not distinguish the kinds of dark matter, so it bears only on V5.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether SAE error vectors are linearly predictable from input activations.
No cross-size comparison of per-token error norms, failed contexts, or whether error vanishes with SAE scale.
The paper reports model cross-entropy after replacing activations with SAE reconstructions, but does not compare the harm with random errors of the same size.
No separation of error into a linearly predictable, not-yet-learned component and a nonlinear component, nor test of further dictionary learning.
Tests whether SAE error nodes contribute to task faithfulness when removed from feature circuits. It does not directly test downstream circuit analysis or steering as separate applications.
No comparison of SAE training objectives or architectures, and no end-to-end training test of whether errors shrink.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Remove residual-stream SAE error nodes from feature circuits and assess faithfulness.
rows.measure: Feature-circuit faithfulness on held-out data
rows.baseline: Feature circuits with SAE error nodes retained
rows.note: The text states that removing residual-stream SAE error nodes severely disrupts the model and curtails maximum performance; the plot provides no extractable numeric value in the supplied text.
rows.check: Wrong condition. Fig. 3 shows circuits with ALL SAE error nodes removed ('w/o SAE errors'), not residual errors alone. The residual-stream attribution is the authors' reading of all-errors vs attn/MLP-only removal. Text: removal 'severely disrupts the model and curtails its maximum performance'. Figure only, no numbers.

source_check.correct: Pythia-70M: Figure 3 compares retained SAE errors with removal of all SAE error nodes, and separately with removal of attention/MLP error nodes. It does not plot residual-error-only removal. Faithfulness magnitudes are figure-only.
source_check.locator_found: §3.2, faithfulness discussion, text lines 659–678; Figure 3 legend and caption.
source_check.problem: The operation and condition incorrectly describe the all-error-removal curve as residual-error-only removal.

relationships.condition: Feature circuits for subject-verb agreement, Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B, with all SAE error nodes removed
relationships.reason: Removing error nodes severely lowers the maximum faithfulness the circuit reaches (r20, r21). Figure-only evidence.
relationships.display_finding: Removing all SAE error nodes severely reduced the maximum circuit faithfulness achieved in Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Feature circuits for subject-verb agreement, Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B, with all SAE error nodes removed
source_check.reason: Figure 3 and §3.2 show substantial disruption and curtailed maximum faithfulness when all errors are removed. This supports meaningful error contributions in the tested circuits; r20 and r21 need their conditions corrected.

relationships.condition: Same circuits with only attention and MLP error nodes removed, residual errors kept
relationships.reason: Reported as less disruptive (r22, r23), so how much function the error carries depends on which component's error is dropped.
relationships.display_finding: Removing only attention and MLP error nodes disrupted circuit faithfulness less than removing all errors while retaining residual errors preserved more function.
